Ruben Amorim is expected to make one change to the starting eleven for Milan-Frosinone, according to the latest reports.

In a recent development, as the international break is over, Milan have used the last couple of days to prepare for Sunday’s clash against Frosinone. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cristiano Ronaldo is now just 14 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals, the landmark he has openly targeted as the defining achievement of the last years of his career.
  • At 41, the question is no longer whether Ronaldo can reach the four-figure mark.
  • The Portuguese superstar remains prolific for Al-Nassr, having taken his tally to 985 with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29th.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo is now just 14 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals, the landmark he has openly targeted as the defining achievement of the last years of his career. It now becomes his final challenge following his announcement that he’ll retire from the Portugal national team.

At 41, the question is no longer whether Ronaldo can reach the four-figure mark. It is how long it will take him to get there.

The Portuguese superstar remains prolific for Al-Nassr, having taken his tally to 985 with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29th.

He recently confirmed that his 23-year international career is over, announcing his decision in an emotional farewell message to Portugal’s supporters.

“The time has come to hang up our national team’s number 7 shirt,” Ronaldo wrote, admitting that it had not been an easy decision.

That leaves Al-Nassr as his only remaining route to the 1,000-goal milestone, barring any change of heart over his international retirement or a farewell appearance for Portugal.

We’ve crunched the numbers and mapped out the various scenarios.

“I want to reach 1,000 goals,” Ronaldo mentioned, unveiling his last major career ambition on Rio Ferdinand’s YouTube channel just over two years ago.

“If I don’t have any injuries, this for me is the most crucial [thing], I want that. For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.

Sources indicate that “All the goals I have scored, they have video. They all have video. Listen, I respect all of them [Pele and Di Stefano]. And if you want more goals, I can bring them from training, too. And I will prove to the people after. They prefer this player, or this is the best one. I don’t care about that.”.

Ronaldo has maintained the importance of that ambition, previously identifying it alongside winning another Nations League title as a major motivation. The latter is now off the table, but his pursuit of four figures remains very much alive.

“Both aims are vital,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that “One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it’s a new age.”.

With all that in mind, here’s our calculations for when Ronaldo could potentially reach the milestone of 1000 goals in his professional career.

– Barring any major career-ending injuries, Ronaldo still looks likely to reach the milestone of a thousand goals at some point in 2027. Possibly as early as January or February, particularly if he maintains his recent scoring form.

Sources indicate that – It’s possible that if Ronaldo enjoys a resurgence and goes on a hot streak akin to his most prolific peak at Real Madrid, he could do it before the end of the year. His goal against Al Ahli took him to 986, leaving him with 14 to find, although his missed penalty in the same game was a reminder that even the most reliable goalscorers have off days. He would still need 14 goals in little over a month, though.

– If you take his recent rate of scoring (27 goals in 42 appearances during the calendar year of 2026) as what he’ll likely maintain, another 22 appearances would be required to score the remaining 14 goals. That would take us through to around February or March 2027. Crucially, that calculation previously allowed for further Portugal appearances, which can no longer be taken for granted.

Industry observers note that – There is an argument that Ronaldo could be set to improve upon that scoring rate. He’s been written off on the international stage after poor showings in the last two major summer tournaments, but he scored eight goals in nine games in the 2024-25 Nations League and a further five goals in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup. Although his international career is now over, rediscover that form in the Saudi Pro League, up his rate to around 1.00 goals per game and fill his boots for Al-Nassr, and Ronaldo could conceivably reach four figures early in 2027. At that rate, he’d need just 14 more appearances.

– There is a counter-argument that Ronaldo will instead slow down in these final furlongs of his career. His latest outing against Al Ahli offered evidence of both sides of that argument: he scored, but also missed a penalty in a 3-1 defeat. His 27 goals in 42 appearances in 2026 work out at 0.64 goals per game. Maintain that rate, and he’ll need another 22 games to score the 14 goals required to reach number one thousand. That should be comfortably achievable before the end of Al-Nassr’s 2026-27 campaign, which is due to end in late May 2027.

– The biggest unknown is now how prolific Ronaldo can remain at club level. His international retirement means he’ll no longer have the opportunity to add goals in Portugal colours, although it should also give him more time to concentrate on Al-Nassr and potentially manage his workload. Whether that makes him even more prolific in Saudi Arabia is another matter.

Recent findings suggest that – What kind of form he’ll show to get there is ultimately anyone’s guess. His goal against Al Ahli was his second in consecutive outings after the hat-trick against Al Kholood, but the missed penalty and defeat offered a less convincing reminder of his current form. The end of his international career removes one variable from our projections, while leaving the exact date far from certain.

– We’ll hedge our bets and estimate that Ronaldo’s form over the coming months will be somewhere between his spectacular peak and a severe decline. He is playing in the Saudi Pro League, after all, and his team is set up to feed him chances. With no more international fixtures to factor into the equation, we’re backing him to keep ticking along for Al-Nassr. With just 14 goals left to score, and having found the net again despite a frustrating evening against Al Ahli, we’re sticking with February 2027 as our tentative prediction for Ronaldo’s 1,000th career goal, although the loss of potential Portugal appearances could yet push that date back.

Gian Piero Gasperini, speaking to DAZN after Parma-Roma (1-5), was pleased with his team’s victory.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot, because there’s always a bit of uncertainty when so many players leave and some return at the last minute. Then you have to figure out if you can pick up where you left off. Today’s result doesn’t reflect how difficult the match was because we faced a very determined Parma side, in excellent condition, who started very strongly. Then, over the 90 minutes, the game took a different turn, but there were moments of great balance.”.

In a recent development, the Grugliasco coach on the final step towards growth: “There are undoubtedly many details, some team-related, some individual, but there’s no doubt that this is a team that’s growing in every aspect. Even in difficult situations, we conceded a bad goal, and there could have been a psychological impact, but instead we reacted very strongly. That’s the best aspect: this team has the confidence to score goals, and even in the face of bad luck, they always have the conviction to move forward.”.

Gian Piero Gasperini on Malen: “But he was still an incredible player even before coming here, just look at his career path, first in Holland and then at Dortmund. You don’t go to certain teams. If you don’t have outstanding qualities, I probably put him where he performs best, not that he didn’t do well at other teams.”.

The Grugliasco-born coach concluded on Serie A forwards and the comparison with the Dutch center-forward: “In the Italian league, the numbers speak for themselves. There’s a great lineup of forwards in Serie A too. Lautaro comes to mind. He’s extraordinary right now and he combines with us. Our team certainly values ​​a striker with these characteristics, perhaps more than another, stronger striker with different characteristics.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 20 November 2026.

Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has revealed his 'unbelievable' experience of working under Allan McGregor.

The former Rangers, Hull and Scotland keeper was brought into the Ibrox backroom staff by Derek McInnes as lead goalkeeping coach in the summer.

Pandur is reaping the benefits of his mentor’s experience and their relationship having kept eight clean sheets during his team’s 12-match unbeaten run.

'It’s unbelievable,' said the Croatian ahead of the Premiership encounter at Motherwell on Saturday night.

'With the career that he had here, he obviously has a lot of experience.

'We have a great relationship where he is my coach, he is my friend. So he’ll tell me when I ask him if I can do something better.

Ivor Pandur has made an impressive start to life at Rangers after joining from Hull City.

'We are here to make each other better. If I can make him a better coach, that’s brilliant. But he’s making me a better goalkeeper and I’m really, really thankful for that.

'Training, first of all, is really, really enjoyable. And he always asks, "What do I want to do? What do I want to improve?". And he’ll give me feedback.

'There’s not a single thing, I would say, that made me better. Just in general, to be able to work in these kind of circumstances and conditions, it’s really enjoyable and it’s making me happy every day.

Sources indicate that 'It’s making me excited to come to work. And that’s because of him also.

'He’s a great guy and he was a great goalkeeper, and it’s enough for me to learn from.'.

Manager McInnes this week described Pandur as a key 'driver' of team culture off the pitch, citing the respect he has from his team-mates.

Pandur, who joined from Hull in the summer, remarked: 'I always want to lead by example. The words are not so notable if you’re not doing your job right.

'So if I can lead by example and show up every day, work as hard as I can, a lot of young players can see that.

Pandur insists he is only going to keep improving under the guidance of Allan McGregor.

'And obviously, I’m always there to help somebody. I was also 19 or 20 and, when I had somebody to learn from, it was much easier.

'Because you get experiences through life and through years of playing, I always try to help everybody else.

'So there are times where I can be more vocal if I feel a need for it, but it’s never my first objective. It’s always to lead by example.'.

Pandur is still awaiting his first international cap but was again away with Croatia this month and he feels meeting the demands of Rangers fans is getting the best out of him.

'It keeps you on your toes,” the former Rijeka, Hellas Verona and Fortuna Sittard player said. 'But in my opinion, pressure is in your head.

'We all play the game we love and we try to do our best. Some days you’ll do good, some days you’ll do bad. We always try to do the right thing.

'Pressure is bigger here, there’s more followers. But it can only make you better because it gets everything out of you.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

Recent findings suggest that in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of fresh signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

Recent findings suggest that in the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

According to recent reports, it could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

Recent findings suggest that “Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] mentioned at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H.

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

According to recent reports, it was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

So we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

Industry observers note that then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Industry observers note that both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the newly introduced order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having stated that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

It looks increasingly as though the Premier League could be a cakewalk for the reigning champions Arsenal – whether or not Manchester City are handed a points deduction.

Man City went into the last international break with a 100% winning record under new manager Enzo Maresca, with it all looking like business as usual following the departure of their era-defining manager Pep Guardiola at the end of last season.

However, things have taken a severe dip after the news broke that the club have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 charges.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein originally broke the news over October’s extended international break, and a few days later the Premier League confirmed it with a statement that could have massive repercussions for the English top flight.

“An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation,” read their statement.

Any potential sanctions are yet to be confirmed or revealed, while Man City have lodged an appeal against the verdict, having stated that they’re “both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission” and continuing to protest their innocence.

In a recent development, city responded in a defiant mood, having extended their winning run by going to Anfield and beating Liverpool 3-0. But a few days later, they were defeated 4-2 to PSG in the Champions League and a serious domestic slump has followed.

Maresca’s men have now suffered three successive Premier League defeats, a run that started with a 2-1 defeat away to Aston Villa. Losses to Brighton and Nottingham Forest followed, before a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham brought that losing streak to an end.

According to recent reports, the result leaves them five points behind Arsenal at this fledgling stage of the Premier League campaign. The Gunners have won nine of their 10 league outings, are consistently keeping clean sheets, and the recent form is ominous.

The question of a points deduction when it comes to a Premier League title race could soon be academic.

City have picked up just seven points from six matches since the verdict was declared in September. That’s eight fewer points than Mikel Arteta’s Gunners, three fewer than Tottenham, and fewer than the likes of Brighton, Bournemouth and Fulham. They are level with Everton.

The shocking Premier League table since Chelsea’s disastrous BlueCo takeover in 2022

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been an interesting and uncertain few years at Chelsea since the BlueCo consortium completed a takeover of the club, ending Roman Abramovich’s ownership after almost two decades.
  • Industry observers note that the Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital-led ownership group inherited one of English football’s most successful clubs.
  • Boehly has since declared his decision to sell his shares and step away from the club, bringing another change to an ownership structure that has rarely been short of headlines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been an interesting and uncertain few years at Chelsea since the BlueCo consortium completed a takeover of the club, ending Roman Abramovich’s ownership after almost two decades.

Industry observers note that the Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital-led ownership group inherited one of English football’s most successful clubs. What followed has been a period of extraordinary spending, managerial upheaval and wildly inconsistent results.

Boehly has since declared his decision to sell his shares and step away from the club, bringing another change to an ownership structure that has rarely been short of headlines. But the bigger question is what BlueCo have actually achieved since taking charge in 2022.

Abramovich was never afraid to sack a manager. There were frequent changes in the dugout during the Russian oligarch’s reign, but silverware was lifted frequently.

There were some lows, including a 10th place finish and trophyless campaign following Jose Mourinho’s meltdown in 2015-16, but generally the club were pretty consistently in the Champions League.

The club only failed to qualify for UEFA’s flagship competition twice during the Abramovich era, and they famously won it twice.

“We are honoured to become the latest custodians of Chelsea Football Club,” new chairman Todd Boehly noted at the time.

In a recent development, “We’re all in – 100% – every minute of every match. Our vision as owners is clear: we want to make the fans proud.

“Along with our commitment to developing the youth squad and acquiring the best talent, our blueprint of action is to invest in the club for the long term and build on Chelsea’s remarkable history of success. I personally want to thank ministers and officials in the British government, and the Premier League, for all their work in making this happen.”.

The upcoming ownership wasted little time making its mark. Thomas Tuchel was sacked, the squad that had lifted the Champions League trophy in 2021 was gradually dismantled, and hundreds of millions were spent on a wholesale rebuild.

Results weren’t immediately forthcoming. Graham Potter struggled to make an impact and Frank Lampard’s return proved a disaster. Chelsea finished 12th in the first year of the BlueCo era – lower than they ever finished in Abramovich’s reign.

There was progress the following year, following further investment and major-money signings like Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez settling in, but Mauricio Pochettino couldn’t quite get them back into the Champions League and departed after just one season.

Industry observers note that year three of BlueCo’s ownership brought further improvements. Enzo Maresca led the Blues to a top-four finish as well as the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup trophies, the latter delivered with a statement 3-0 victory over European champions PSG in the final.

However, it doesn’t appear that progress has been linear. Maresca departed in January, Chelsea limply exited the Champions League at the Round of 16, and his successor Liam Rosenior struggled badly for results.

A dire run cost the young coach his job after only a few months at the helm, while the financial implications of failing to qualify for Europe brought into sharp focus the viability of this entire project.

While individual seasons have offered reasons for optimism, the bigger picture makes for less comfortable reading.

Sources indicate that looking at the Premier League table since BlueCo took over, Chelsea have collected 244 points from 163 matches. That’s only eighth in the division, behind Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Aston Villa, Newcastle, Manchester United and Brighton.

They have won just 68 of those 163 games, with 55 defeats. Brighton, a club who have received a reported £265million from Chelsea for players, managers and staff, have actually collected two more points over the same period.

Chelsea are also 115 points behind Arsenal. The gap has become a chasm.

According to recent reports, there have been some truly miserable afternoons along the way, too. Chelsea’s historic home defeats to Tottenham and Leeds this season are particularly difficult to reconcile with the club’s former standards. Losing to either rival at Stamford Bridge would once have been a major embarrassment. Losing to both underlines just how much has changed, and the pressure already mounting on Xabi Alonso.

Here’s the full table since BlueCo completed a takeover of the club.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Conte had been heavily linked with the role at Old Trafford, joining Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Unai Emery among the list bookmakers' favourites to replace Michael Carrick.

Man United ultimately went with another former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in Mauricio Pochettino, paying around £10million in compensation to lure him away from being head coach of the United States' national team.

Conte, who remains out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer, has now hit back at reports suggesting Man United may have been put off by his intensity and demands.

'First, let me address the question of my method,' Conte told the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast.

Recent findings suggest that 'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Man United opted to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick.

Conte hit back at suggestions Man United's hierachy might have been relucant to appoint him because of his methods.

'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

Sources indicate that '(United) last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson.

'I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football, though, at times, his Scottish accent can be quite hard to follow.

'Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great.

'That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

According to recent reports, 'A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.'.

Conte has long been known for his combustible personality - as well as an impressive winning record as a coach.

Recent findings suggest that at Chelsea, he fell out with star striker Diego Costa, centre back David Luiz and the club's board. At Napoli, he left a year after winning the Serie A title and mentioned there was 'too much poison, too much malice' at the club.

Conte has developed a reputation for his high intensity and demands, while the Italian famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference attacking the club's culture.

Conte has won five Serie A titles across three clubs and won the Premier League with Chelsea.

Conte famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference in 2023, where he labelled his players as 'selfish' and took aim at the club's culture.

The Italian, however, has overseen five Serie A title wins during his spells at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, along with winning the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea.

It is not the first time Conte has spoken out in recent weeks following links to Old Trafford, with the 57-year-old having denied he had set 'specific conditions' about taking over at United.

La Repubblica claimed Conte wanted 'carte blanche on the transfer market' and to act as a manager, rather than a head coach, with a technical staff behind the scenes chosen by him involving 'trusted collaborators'.

'My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,' Conte responded on social media last month.

'Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

According to recent reports, 'I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

'Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.'.

Pochettino, who landed the job at Old Trafford, has faced a whirlwind start having flown into Manchester following his final match in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

The Argentine took training for the first time on Thursday and will lead the Red Devils out for the first time on Sunday in a blockbuster clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino takes over with Man United lying in the Premier League's relegation zone having won just one of their opening ten matches.

#71747. Bayern Munich’s treatment of Jamal Musiala is grim, depressing and utterly classless

Bayern Munich’s treatment of Jamal Musiala is grim, depressing and utterly classless

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are few things more exciting than watching an academy graduate develop into a superstar.
  • He joined the club as a 16-year-old, grew into a world-class talent, has made over 200 first-team appearances and won six Bundesliga titles.
  • According to recent reports, so how did we get here?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are few things more exciting than watching an academy graduate develop into a superstar. Bayern Munich got to experience exactly that with Jamal Musiala.

He joined the club as a 16-year-old, grew into a world-class talent, has made over 200 first-team appearances and won six Bundesliga titles. For a time, he was the envy of Europe. It was only a couple of years ago that he was widely regarded as one of the finest young talents in the world.

According to recent reports, so how did we get here? To a situation where Bayern’s hierarchy seem intent on unsettling one of their most valuable players and making his position at the club increasingly uncomfortable.

“We’re in a dilemma with him,” honorary president Uli Hoeness told BILD a couple of weeks ago.

Sources indicate that “He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, but can be managed to some extent with medication. However, whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had remains uncertain.”.

In a recent development, to understand the situation, you have to appreciate just how much Musiala has been through. His momentum was first halted by a devastating ACL injury at the 2025 Club World Cup, which saw him sidelined for half a season. He hasn’t quite ever recaptured his best form since returning to action.

Industry observers note that there have been further complications, too. Musiala revealed in August that he was being treated for a neurological dysfunction which causes temporary seizures, following two collapses during Bayern’s pre-season friendlies.

“The experience with such an injury suggests that it will be difficult for him to reach the level he had before,” Bayern legend Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has since stoked the fire.

Industry observers note that “His high salary is no longer sustainable. Nobody will buy him under these conditions. The discussion hasn’t taken place yet, but we have to think about the finances.”.

It has been revealed that it is difficult to escape the feeling that Bayern’s hierarchy are turning the screw. German outlet BILD have subsequently reported that Musiala’s medication continues to cause problems, with recurring side effects proving problematic. Whether coincidental or otherwise, the steady drip-feed of negative headlines is doing little for the player.

Industry observers note that bayern have already made Harry Kane Europe’s highest-paid player and are reportedly keen to reward Michael Olise with a bumper newly introduced deal. The prospect of having Musiala on similarly astronomical wages is said to be a headache for the Bayern hierarchy.

Recent findings suggest that that is hardly Musiala’s problem. Contracts work both ways, and Bayern cannot expect players to honour their commitments only when it suits the club financially. They were happy to offer him those wages in the first place.

FIFPRO is the global representative organisation for professional footballers’ unions, advocating for players’ rights, welfare and working conditions around the world. They have struck the perfect tone.

“FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich’s leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury,” they posted in a statement.

In a recent development, “Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.

“Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

Sources indicate that “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise. Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.

“FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same.”.

In a recent development, they’ve absolutely nailed it. We couldn’t have put it better ourselves.

Bayern’s old guard are entitled to their opinions, but we’re equally entitled to call out behaviour that is utterly classless. Musiala is going through a horrible experience, battling a difficult medical condition while trying to get his career back on track – all the while feeling like his club doesn’t have his back.

Sources indicate that borussia Dortmund are top of the Bundesliga. Long may that continue as Bayern continue this sorry spectacle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.
  • Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.
  • Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” stated Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

According to recent reports, “I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

In a recent development, sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

According to recent reports, he told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a massive difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

According to recent reports, palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It’s been quite the ride for Leeds since their return to the Premier League, but they comfortably stayed up last season and are now looking increasingly established at this level.
  • In the opening months of the 2025-26 campaign, Farke struggled to balance attack and defence as his side only took 11 points from their first 12 matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since Leeds United switched to a 3-5-2 formation, only a handful of Premier League clubs have accumulated more points than Daniel Farke’s side.

It’s been quite the ride for Leeds since their return to the Premier League, but they comfortably stayed up last season and are now looking increasingly established at this level.

In the opening months of the 2025-26 campaign, Farke struggled to balance attack and defence as his side only took 11 points from their first 12 matches.

During those first 12 games, Leeds often lined up in a 4-3-3 formation, which often left them looking vulnerable in defence.

With Leeds sat in the bottom three and Farke under increasing pressure, he made the switch to 3-5-2 during their trip to Manchester City in November.

While Leeds lost that game in the last minute thanks to a Phil Foden winner, Farke’s side demonstrated a competitive edge that they had been lacking in several of their previous games.

Since then, the German boss has stuck with the 3-5-2 formation and Leeds’ league form has taken a huge leap forward as a result.

It has been revealed that they went on a seven-game unbeaten streak in the Premier League immediately afterwards, which was their longest undefeated top-flight streak since 2001. They’ve since beaten that with an even longer unbeaten run.

Leeds went on to comfortably secure their Premier League status last season, and they’ve continued to build on that progress in 2026-27.

Farke’s side have established themselves in mid-table, currently sitting eighth with 50 points from 36 matches. They’ve lost just twice this season, although a tendency to draw games has prevented them from making a sustained push towards the European places.

In the Championship, Farke often stuck to his 4-2-3-1 formation, but conceded that he needed to be more adaptable in the Premier League.

“When we were winning most games [last season], we did not change our base formation much,” Farke told Sky Sports last season.

“The top teams in Europe and the Premier League always play the same formation.

Recent findings suggest that “But you have to bridge this gap of individual quality, you have to be more flexible. This was clear at the beginning of the season. For that, we have trained a lot in a three-man formation. I knew we are prepared to switch between it in each and every game.”.

Farke’s side have now produced a stunning 4-1 away victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing their first win at the ground in decades and underlining their credentials as a serious Premier League outfit.

That result adds further weight to the argument that the switch to 3-5-2 has transformed Leeds, with their remarkable resilience making them an increasingly difficult side to beat.

To illustrate just how good Leeds have been since the end of November 2025, here is the Premier League table since they switched to a 3-5-2 formation.

  • It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026.

Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.

It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.

Which is why any talk of the Edinburgh club experiencing some sort of mini-revival should quite rightly be taken with more than a large pinch of salt.

Let’s not forget, at the start of the month, newly introduced boss Marink Reedijk had picked up a paltry point from his four games in charge since taking the reins from David Gray.

Performances weren’t up to much either.

A statement win over Hearts at Hampden to book their Premier Sports Cup final spot was backed up with an emphatic 4-0 dismantling of Aberdeen up at Pittodrie.

Hibs manager Marink Reedijk is still searching for his first victory at Easter Road.

Credit where it’s due, of course. Both victories were hard-earned and thoroughly deserved.

In a recent development, but it’s important not to read too much in to either of them. Players going above and beyond in a derby clash should be a given, while the Dons appeared to have chucked it altogether under the stewardship of former manager Stephen Robinson long before Hibs turned up in the Granite City.

The real test begins this weekend with the visit of Dundee United, as Reedijk’s men look to secure a first home Premiership win in over seven months.

It has been revealed that the fans have been crying out for entertainment in Leith for far longer than that. In the latter days of Gray’s reign, the atmosphere at Easter Road was verging on toxic.

Reedijk needs to change that, and now has two games against the Dundee clubs over the next four days to get the momentum swinging in the opposite direction.

Continuing to get the best out of his midfield three will be key to that.

Recent findings suggest that the reintroduction of Joe Newell to the starting XI has paid off big-time. Not so much in terms of the stats, but rather what he allows Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan to do.

The former was linked with a move to Celtic over the summer, but looked miles off it in the early weeks of the campaign until Newell lined up alongside him.

Chaiwa can be guilty of trying to carry out too many jobs in the middle of the park, but Newell’s calming influence has enabled him to stick to what he’s good at — namely breaking up the play and moving the ball on to his more creative team-mates in front of him.

There’s no doubt the Zambian is at his best when he keeps things simple.

Joe Newell has provided a calming influence in the middle of the park amid this upturn in form.

It has been revealed that newell’s presence has also freed Mulligan to play further up the field rather than on the fringes of his own box, where he was popping up far too often a couple of months ago. He’s wasted back there.

If he can add some more goals and assists to his name over the next few, there is every chance he can play himself in to the thoughts of Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli ahead of the next set of internationals.

It should be an intriguing battle this afternoon in the engine room, with United boasting the most cohesive midfield group in the top flight with Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal.

Of course, even if Hibs deliver in that sense, it may count for very little if the guys at the top end of the pitch can’t do the business. The lack of cutting edge has been an ongoing concern. Four goals against Aberdeen doesn't change that.

Owen Elding appears to be Reedijk’s preferred option in the central striker role, but while the young Irishman has shown flashes of his potential, he has offered little to suggest he can be relied upon to find the net on a consistent basis.

The problem is, can anyone? Record-signing Thibault Klidje may have opened his league account for the season against the Dons, however we’ve seen enough to know that he isn’t the answer.

Ante Suto is in the same boat, while Stoke City loanee Nathan Lowe has struggled for both game time and form.

And as for Rabbi Matondo? Well, the wait goes on to see any real return on that investment. Early days, mind you.

That Martin Boyle remains Hibs’ main goalscoring threat is troubling, especially given that the veteran can’t even be considered a nailed-on starter these days.

Sources indicate that there are a significant number of players — across all areas of the park — fighting for their future at the club. Indeed, you would imagine Reedijk is counting down the days until January when he will look to freshen up the squad with guys more suited to his style.

Lyall Cameron has been a key man behind Dundee United's surge up the Premiership table.

Hibs should use today’s opponents as an example of how patience can pay off.

According to recent reports, it’s fair to say that Jim Goodwin has never been Mr. Popular in and around Tannadice. Goodness knows why.

Many fans were calling for his head as recently as the summer after failing to secure a top-six finish last term, but he is slowly but surely starting to win over his doubters.

Make no mistake, this season presents a golden opportunity for United to seriously challenge for third spot.

You never know what you’re going to get from Hearts on any given week, while this is very much uncharted territory for Falkirk.

And let’s face it, nobody would expect the likes of Hibs, Aberdeen or Motherwell to claw themselves into contention.

While everyone else tries to stumble their way through a period of transition, United’s consistency – both on and off the park – could prove to be the difference.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

Industry observers note that this was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”.

According to recent reports, asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso mentioned: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

According to recent reports, “We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”.

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding latest ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0.

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Industry observers note that already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

In a recent development, chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv.

Sources indicate that that should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

In a recent development, he signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

In a recent development, bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

In a recent development, chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

It has been revealed that yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

In a recent development, next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

According to recent reports, for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

In a recent development, the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Industry observers note that keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews noted. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

In a recent development, brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

Industry observers note that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

In a recent development, it was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

In a recent development, any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very key points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

It has been revealed that the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” remarked Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca stated in his pre-match press conference.”.

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”.

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

According to recent reports, elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Recent findings suggest that breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

It has been revealed that pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

Tech Report: Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The new Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1337 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their fresh manager.
  • Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their fresh manager.

Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.

As is usually the case these days, much about the modern United remains unclear.

But what we do know after welcoming the eighth full-time manager since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson is that once again England’s biggest football club is relying on a personality lift to drag them back to their feet.

This is what happens when you get things wrong for so long, when you buy the wrong players and install executives who appear to be learning on the job. You end up hiring and firing managers, waiting for the one who finally arrives with the magic dust, the capacity to somehow create something greater than the sum of the rather wonky parts.

Listening to Pochettino here – a talented coach and a good person – was to occasionally think back to words spoken in the weeks of their arrivals on this territory by predecessors such as Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

For they too were asked about such intangibles as culture and mood and philosophy. They too were asked about more prosaic football matters such as match fitness.

It’s a conversational cycle that tells a story of recurring and systematic football failure.

Mauricio Pochettino faced reporters in his first press conference as Manchester United boss on Friday.

A drone captured footage of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday.

Amorim – back on a grim, foggy day exactly two years ago – was asked about Marcus Rashford and whether he had been right to spend time off in New York days before the new United manager walked through the door.

Here, Pochettino could justifiably have been asked about another forward Bryan Mbeumo spending the wee hours of Thursday morning playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto video game when he probably should have been asleep.

This is the United that Pochettino is now being asked to fix, a club where names and faces change but problems remain the same.

The Berrada interview was actually more enlightening than Pochettino’s carefully managed introduction to the wider media.

Certainly it was interesting to listen to his assertion that nine defensive players in one squad was enough. In football, as United are discovering yet again, it’s not necessarily the quantity that matters but the quality.

One point did resonate rather more deeply, though, and that was the one Berrada – once of Manchester City – made about United’s players needing a manager capable of dealing with the scrutiny of the club and who could shield some of his players from all that comes with it.

The recently-departed Michael Carrick did look rather lost on the touchline in the final tumultuous weeks of his time as manager. He didn’t look an awful lot more comfortable in front of the TV cameras either.

Bryan Mbeumo posted this picture after the midnight release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Sources indicate that in the dressing room? Well, he lost the loyalty of his captain Bruno Fernandes towards the end and that is never a good sign.

Sources indicate that pochettino will do rather better at all that. The former Chelsea, PSG and Tottenham manager has a personality and a charisma that could fill an aircraft hangar. His players will arrive at Anfield for his opening game on Sunday feeling better about themselves than they have for some time.

United have hired some confidence and some authority and some experience at a time when they desperately need it, even if Berrada’s claim that they had to call the USA Federation last week to check on his release clause suggested this is an appointment made rather on the hoof.

It is, however, the impact that Pochettino can bring over time on a jumbled squad put together for six different managers over an incredible 12 years that will define him. Here, the 54-year-old undoubtedly faces challenges.

Talking this week to someone associated with Tottenham about Pochettino’s progressive seasons there between 2014 and 2019, I was reminded of the quality that the Argentinian was given to work with.

Pochettino's Spurs side harnessed the attacking power of stars including Harry Kane and Heung-min Son.

The French international goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris, the Belgian central defensive partnership of Toby Alderweireld and Jan Vertonghen, England international defenders Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Kieran Trippier and, further forward, the burgeoning attacking talents of Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, Heung-min Son and Harry Kane.

It was a prototype Premier League football team, both in talent, age, fitness and physicality. That was why, in 2016, it almost won it.

Pochettino does not have this at Old Trafford. He doesn’t have anything like it. He has some talented players. The fact he inherits a team in the bottom three is down to Carrick’s inadequacies.

But this United squad is a mish-mash and it serves a purpose to ask how many would get in that old Spurs team we talk about.

Industry observers note that fernandes? Maybe. Mbeumo? Probably. That is about it and that, frankly, is where United are right now.

Industry observers note that pochettino has long wanted this job. It’s not a posting of convenience for him. Like others before him – men like Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal – he has long since coveted the cachet, the stature and the power of this remarkable football institution.

Mourinho and Van Gaal had better players than Pochettino is being handed and they both still failed, largely because they were shown to be coaches already over the top of that hill that both had worked so desperately hard to climb.

Mbeumo is one of the few United players who might have got into Pochettino's Spurs side.

Industry observers note that where does Pochettino sit in terms of his own personal and professional growth? That is such a hard question to answer and will be utterly fundamental to how he travels in the weeks and months to come.

Sitting here fresh from the training ground and strangely seeming to question whether the glass of water in front of him was fit to drink, Pochettino declared himself to be in his coaching prime.

‘I am a much better coach now,’ he mentioned.

The proof or otherwise of that will only be revealed out on the grass. For all that he can plead valid mitigation, Pochettino was not hugely impressive in Paris or at Stamford Bridge. Before he starts to talk about dysfunctional football clubs, he may wish to take a look at his fresh surroundings.

In a recent development, liverpool away feels like something of a free hit. Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday less so and Brentford at home next Saturday definitely not. And so it begins. A run of 12 games in six and a half weeks that may well see Pochettino crawling into January begging for fresh legs and newly introduced players.

The new manager said here that he wishes to be across transfers and little wonder. When he looks at the mistakes made in that regard by a succession of United regimes and executives, he may indeed question what it is they put in the water in the north-west.

It has been revealed that united fans will perhaps appreciate that one of the ‘higher ups’ at Old Trafford has finally put his head above the parapet, even if they question some of what Berrada mentioned. That’s been overdue.

It has been revealed that in terms of their newly introduced manager, they can be forgiven for keeping a lid on any excitement. Many of them have simply been wearied by the cycle.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

It has been revealed that this has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

Industry observers note that this was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

Johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa in front! 🟣 https://t.co/jxZf2568Sl.

According to recent reports, it is getting hard to comprehend what Jaissle wants his team to do. The much-hyped “vertical” style looks like an ugly incarnation of the long ball football of yesteryear. They did not like it at Newcastle in the 1980s and 1990s and some fashions should never return. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

There is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Newcastle are not getting better; they are making all the same mistakes and, if anything, as an attacking force, they are looking increasingly stale and predictable. They did not have a shot on target in the first half and, other than one fantastic save in the second, Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki had nothing to do.

Industry observers note that it is time for a sharp dose of medicine on Tyneside. Expectations need to be adjusted, especially as none of the new signings have impressed. This was always the fear and the risk when you put all your faith in young players from abroad.

For Jaissle’s vertical football to work, Newcastle need to be able to win the ball high up the pitch, whether that is with a high press or competing for second balls from long passes. They do not do either well. More worryingly, they look so vulnerable, so easy to play through.

Villa did it to them all afternoon. Nicolas Jackson should have scored in the first half, Ibrahim Mbaye should have hit the target in the second.
