  • Industry observers note that the room is abuzz.
  • In a recent development, goalkeeper Lee and five of his Everton Under-21s teammates have gleefully taken up the task of being reading buddies to the children of Ellesmere Port’s Meadow Primary School, one of six schools that make up the recently renamed Everton Multi-Academy Trust (EMAT).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Captain Underpants”. The laughter that follows is infectious. It seems doubtful that it was an honest answer to the question posed to Zach Lee by the young boy located somewhere near the front of the classroom: “What is your favourite book?” But it got exactly the reaction he was after.

Industry observers note that the room is abuzz. It has been for much of the past hour.

In a recent development, goalkeeper Lee and five of his Everton Under-21s teammates have gleefully taken up the task of being reading buddies to the children of Ellesmere Port’s Meadow Primary School, one of six schools that make up the recently renamed Everton Multi-Academy Trust (EMAT). Seven miles away, six of their Under-21 peers are doing likewise at Oldfield Primary School in Chester.

Nearer to Liverpool, the hollers that greeted Everton Women’s Holly McNamara and Karen Holmgaard 24 hours earlier are still reverberating around the corridors of Bidston Avenue Primary School.

According to recent reports, christian Nørgaard and close friends Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George are also familiar with the noise the pupils at the Birkenhead school can make. Last month, the trio were serenaded with a ukulele rendition of Spirit of the Blues on a visit there. Blue ukuleles, of course.

If the colour of the musical instruments is a cute indicator of the strengthening ties between the football club and the EMAT schools, the time being spared by the players is of much greater significance.

It is intended to demonstrate a cross-Club connection with EMAT, which sits alongside Everton in the Community as one of Everton’s associated organisations. “Part of the Everton family,” as Everton’s Chief Tax and Sustainability Officer and Chair of Trustees for EMAT Alison Haynes puts it.

Recent findings suggest that but there is a deeper intention, too. “We want to use the power of the Everton crest to inspire and engage youngsters in education,” notes Steven Baker OBE, CEO of EMAT. Baker has seen this in evidence for more than a decade, having previously served as Principal of Everton Alternative Provision Free School, the award-winning L4 facility that offers youngsters who have struggled in mainstream schools a route back into education.

Lee and his Under-21 colleagues, McNamara and Holmgaard are all supporting one particular mission of EMAT - to inspire youngsters towards a life-long love of reading. More immediately, to ensure they have the requisite literacy level to adequately prepare them for what lies ahead in secondary school education.

It has been revealed that in Ellesmere Port, Chester and Birkenhead, the players are tackling their role head on. Books - donated by Everton staff to help replenish the schools’ libraries - are strewn across the tables and spilling onto the floor. No-one’s troubled by the mess.

Industry observers note that julia Donaldson’s greatest hits are being played out across the room. Michael Morpurgo – a childhood favourite author of midfielder Jack Patterson – can be heard, too. ‘Bluey’ is an appropriately named hit on another table. And then there’s Lee and a group of little ones giggling at Captain Underpants.

Close by to the classroom at Meadow, Everton’s leading post-war goalscorer Graeme Sharp is here too, continuing the literacy theme by officially opening the school’s newly-refurbished library.

According to recent reports, “These children will remember today,” says Baker. “They will remember players from Everton coming into school and taking the time to sit with them.

Industry observers note that “They love hearing stories but they also love having someone to read to. Both aspects are so important for a child’s development.”.

As is music. It’s why Dibling, George and Norgaard found themselves being taught the chords to one of Goodison’s – and now Hill Dickinson Stadium’s – favourite tunes last month.

Studies show a direct correlation between a child mastering a musical instrument and making their mark in maths and other creative fields.

The Toffees trio left behind gifts of recorders (blue ones), helping the school expand the opportunities it can offer to its pupils.

“We find it’s really notable for their resilience and it's good for the children mentally and socially to have the opportunity to not only play an instrument, but to play to an audience,” indicates Bidston Avenue headteacher Stuart Brady, a Tranmere Rovers fan.

Sources indicate that “It's great for us as a school to have the connection we do with Everton and the players. Days like this are great, but it's also about the children feeling they belong to something bigger.”.

And the proof that EMAT is getting it right is stacking up. In 2024, Everton Free School and Everton Football College – the two original schools on which the Trust was founded – were jointly awarded an ‘Outstanding’ rating by Ofsted. Earlier this year, the respected national TES Awards named EMAT (then The People’s Learning Trust) as its Trust of the Year for trusts with nine schools or fewer.

With the support of a Premier League football club and its players behind them, it is hoped the collective will continue to go from strength to strength.

Recent findings suggest that the intention is that Everton’s Under-21s will return to the schools to resume their reading buddy duties at junctures throughout the season, strengthening their bonds with the schools and pupils. It is seen as a vital part of the players’ professional development.

Recent findings suggest that representatives from the Men’s and Women’s team will continue to play their part also. Merlin Röhl has already been a guest of Oldfield Primary School’s after-school chess club, taking up an invitation to share his love of the ancient game with the next generation.

“We understand the responsibility and influence we have as a football club when it comes to our communities,” indicates Haynes. “And you cannot understate the impact the player visits have.

“The atmosphere and the smiles you see in the room, the energy they give to the children… it’s truly wonderful.”.

Cesc Fabregas praised Jacobo Ramón’s attacking threat after the defender scored in Como’s 2-0 win over Cagliari, although he insisted the performance was far from perfect.

In a recent development, with quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, Ramón headed Como in front from Yan Couto’s assist in the 24th minute, and Lucas Da Cunha added a second, also set up by Couto, early in the second half. The win takes Fabregas’ side up to fourth for now, and Como remain unbeaten at the Sinigaglia in Serie A this season.

In a recent development, “Perfect? No. We conceded four counter-attacks, three of them big chances where they could have scored,” Fabregas noted. “They did something different going forward and found space in behind us, but from around the 35th minute things changed, and in the second half there was only one team on the pitch.

Sources indicate that “I’m very happy for the lads. There was so much energy, and Lahdo came on very well. We had to finish with two right-backs because we don’t have the players. Today my only attacking option on the bench was Nico Paz.”.

Ramón has just been called up by Spain for the first time, and Fabregas believes his scoring has improved a lot.

Industry observers note that “There are players who are stronger, but he’s a player I like. I won’t say too much about how I feel about him, because he might read it later,” Fabregas joked. “We worked a lot on his finishing. Last year he couldn’t score in front of goal, even easy chances. Now he scores them. It demonstrates you they’re kids, but they improve every year.

In the air, he’s first or second in Serie A for duels won. “In five or six years, I’d like to see all these lads playing at World Cups and winning the Champions League. They have the chance to grow here.”.

Da Cunha started despite his efforts with France this week, because Maxence Caqueret picked up a minor problem on Friday.

“Honestly, I wanted to rest him today, but we can’t take risks now, we’re down to 11, 12, 13 players. He’s a gem for us. He always raises the level. I’d like every player in the world to have Da Cunha’s mentality.”.

“There are seven games left before Christmas, and everyone has to play their part.”.

Paris Saint-Germain fear Désiré Doue has suffered a serious knee injury, a fresh blow for Luis Enrique days before Roma visit the Parc des Princes in the Champions League.

According to Foot Mercato, the 21-year-old’s right knee gave way while he was shielding the ball, with no contact from an opponent, late in the first half of Saturday’s Ligue 1 game at Nice. He had scored to make it 2-1 only minutes earlier.

Recent findings suggest that doué left the pitch in tears on a stretcher and was replaced by Ferran Torres. PSG are waiting for scans to confirm how serious the injury is, but Foot01 report that the club fear a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament.

If confirmed, it would be a second major knee injury in barely a month for the European champions. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the ACL in his right knee in October’s 4-2 win over Barcelona and is expected to miss most of the season. Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also suffered thigh injuries in that game.

Doué had only just returned from an earlier injury when he joined up with France this month.

PSG are chasing a third consecutive Champions League title, and they host Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma on Wednesday at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT]. Whatever the scans show, Doué is very unlikely to face the Giallorossi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur recorded three successive home Premier League wins for the first time in two years as they swept Ipswich Town aside on Saturday afternoon.

Tottenham were looking to bounce back from a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Leeds United at Elland Road before the international break, and Roberto De Zerbi made the substantial call to hand 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett his first competitive start for the club on the left wing.

Spurs fans have long been calling to see the teenager handed a start after what they had seen from the youngster in pre-season and in glimpses off the substitutes' bench this term, and his Italian manager decided to blood him in the absence of the injured Mathys Tel.

It was still a major decision given Dejan Kulusevski, Omar Marmoush and Savio were named on the substitutes' bench, but he repaid his manager's faith with a stunning display that will surely see him retain his spot against Sunderland next Sunday.

Williams-Barnett took just 15 minutes to open his account for the club as he finished from close range following a fine cross from the right by Pedro Porro, before assisting Dominic Solanke's goal in the second half following a low ball in from the left flank.

The 18-year-old was a huge threat throughout his 64 minutes on the pitch, and mucked in from a defensive point of view as well to help the team keep a clean sheet.

Williams-Barnett for Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Williams-Barnett will take all the plaudits, and rightly so, but his teammate Porro was also influential in the victory against the Tractor Boys.

In a summer when Tottenham paid £100m to sign a player, and brought in nine more, arguably their best bit of summer business was tying Porro down to a upcoming long-term contract at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Fresh on the back of winning the World Cup with Spain, there would have been concerns that the 27-year-old would attract interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs, especially after interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid previously.

However, Porro had already committed his future to Spurs by penning a five-year deal in June, extending his stay in North London even though the club only escaped relegation to the Championship on the final day of last season.

There have been a few ups and downs in terms of his performances this term, including a poor outing against Leeds last time out, but the Spaniard was back to his best and on top form against Ipswich.

As we mentioned previously, it was his cross that gave Williams-Barnett his first goal in a Tottenham shirt, and his display led to him actually being given a higher rating than the teenager on Fotmob (8.3 compared to 8.1).

He did everything he could to help Spurs in the final third, while he also completed his defensive duties to help the hosts keep a clean sheet.

Tottenham have made a massive improvement after a tough start to the season under De Zerbi's leadership, and there is no doubt that they look a much better team when Porro is on his game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today, as of 10:16 GMT, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has journeyed one light-day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any human-made object has gone before. At this distance, signals from Earth’s surface travelling at light speed will take a full 24 hours to reach the craft. The trailblazing probe is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029, when its plutonium power finally dies. But that time might not signal the end of Voyager 1’s contributions — the craft carries a golden record engraved with sights and sounds from Earth, an interspecies message for any aliens who might encounter it as it continues its journey.

A device that stimulates the brain with flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds has failed to slow memory loss in people with Alzheimer’s disease. The Spectris AD headset is designed to induce brain activity called gamma waves, which have been linked to increased attention and memory. The results of a long-anticipated clinical trial demonstrated that participants who used the device did not show robust improvements in their cognitive function after a year of treatment compared with those assigned to a sham treatment. The results were reported at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease meeting on 16 November.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has revealed that the United States has lost its measles elimination status amid an outbreak that’s caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year. The US had eliminated measles in 2000 after an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates in the past few years have left pockets of the population vulnerable to infection. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” notes virologist Paul Offit. Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO announced.

Source: International Vaccine Access Center, Johns Hopkins University.

Consumer tests that promise to reveal the full range of microbes living in your gut are taking off — but their results can vary widely. “This is an industry that’s running wild,” notes genomicist Jacques Ravel, who co-authored a study that tested several providers. With regard to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”. But it’s hard to set those standards, writes journalist Amber Dance, who sent off her own stool to investigate the field. Part of the problem is that “there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample”, she says.

Recent findings suggest that the proportion of reviewers at Nature who are early-career researchers. Increasing it would benefit all researchers and science as a whole, argues a Nature editorial. (Nature | 6 min read).

It has been revealed that amid the tedium of investigating potentially fraudulent papers, “there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers”, writes research-integrity sleuth Dorothy Bishop. Bishop and Nature’s careers team have compiled a quiz to test your ability to match ‘tortured phrases’ — those that replace common words with synonyms in an attempt to skirt past plagiarism-detection software — with their original text.

Industry observers note that from the Bering Strait to Doggerland, much of human history occurred in places that are now underwater, covered by the sea-level rise that occurs after ice ages. Geographer Jerome Dobson has dubbed this drowned land ‘Aquaterra’. It’s the site of many discoveries — such as Blinkerwall in the Baltic Sea, one of Europe’s oldest and largest Stone Age structures — and possibly many more to come. It also offers an interesting thought experiment: if we continue to drive global warming, what might future archaeologists make of our inundated world?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Daniel Farke's side came out of the international break with a superb performance as they hit back immediately from going a goal down to dominate the rest of the proceedings on the way to a 4-1 victory.
  • It was the visitors' first win at Stamford Bridge this century and saw United overtake their hosts in the Premier League table as they climbed to sixth, thanks to an Okafor brace, a penalty from Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Brenden Aaronson's late fourth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attacking standouts such as Noah Okafor will take the headlines after Leeds United dismantled Chelsea at Stamford Bridge but the man who unlocked that performance deserves just as many accolades.

Daniel Farke's side came out of the international break with a superb performance as they hit back immediately from going a goal down to dominate the rest of the proceedings on the way to a 4-1 victory.

It was the visitors' first win at Stamford Bridge this century and saw United overtake their hosts in the Premier League table as they climbed to sixth, thanks to an Okafor brace, a penalty from Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Brenden Aaronson's late fourth.

Emmanuel Emegha had opened the scoring in the 25th minute with his first goal for Chelsea, but Okafor cancelled it out moments later as he slid the equaliser into the far corner with the Blues' defence panicking as he entered the box.

Michael Oliver awarded Leeds a penalty early in the second half when a shot was blocked by Morgan Rogers' arm, with insufficient evidence available to VAR to say whether it had hit him above the T-shirt line and whether they could overturn it, with Calvert-Lewin stepping up to send Emi Martinez the wrong way.

Okafor doubled the lead just five minutes later to effectively end the contest, slamming into the top corner from a deflected ball across the area, and substitute Aaronson rounded things off in stoppage time as he surged clear and cut inside before slipping the ball between Martinez's legs.

But as impressive as the Whites were in attack, the game was won in midfield, where Chelsea lost Moises Caicedo to injury mid-way through the first half and subsequently failed to regain any sort of control.

It is difficult to pick just one from Leeds' central midfield pairing of ex-Blue Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka, but the Japanese international was outstanding on the day.

The Yorkshire Evening Post rated him 9/10 following the final whistle, and it wasn't hard to see why after his excellent work in and out of possession, particularly as his side took charge after the break.

Tanaka was ably supported by Ampadu as they took full advantage of Chelsea losing one of their £100 million men, leaving replacement Jordan Henderson, and Romeo Lavia, over-matched in the middle.

As is so often the case on Leeds' best days under Farke, including on previous occasions against the same opposition, Tanaka was the heartbeat of the side as he moved the ball around efficiently and didn't give his opposite numbers time to think.

Stats compiled by FotMob indicate the 28-year-old was highly effective with his 59 touches across 86 minutes on the pitch, as he bounced back from a series of early fouls conceded to shine as the game went on.

With the ball at his feet, Tanaka kept Leeds moving efficiently, completing 43 of his 49 passes, and wasn't dispossessed once on the day, while his defensive contributions also made a real difference.

The Leeds man made a pair of successful tackles, two interceptions, and seven recoveries of possession, and wasn't dribbled past once as part of an excellent display all round.

Chelsea simply couldn't put together enough passes to threaten getting back into the game as Tanaka and his teammates didn't give them the time or space to regroup, while operating with far more zip when going the other way.

Okafor's finishes will deservedly take much of the focus, but the attacking platform provided by the midfield was vital, just as it was in ensuring James Trafford was relatively untested at the back.

A first Stamford Bridge win since 1999 appeared to be on the cards earlier this season when Farke took his side to West London in the Carabao Cup, only for it to be snatched away during a chaotic second half in September.

Leeds led 2-0 at the break before a Cole Palmer penalty sparked a turnaround which resulted in a 6-3 Chelsea victory and extended the run without a victory at this ground by one more game.

It was very much the reverse on Saturday afternoon as the hosts this time went ahead but collapsed themselves following the interval to see Farke and his players depart with a vital three points.

And on current evidence it is unlikely to be another 27 years until Leeds get another win away at one of their old rivals.

According to recent reports, he is yet to play a single minute of competitive senior football but he is clear on what he wishes to become. Among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten New Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

After detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, remarked.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the fresh campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

In a recent development, tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” stated Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#71650. EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm

EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1175 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation.
  • Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.
  • Industry observers note that the European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation. These include a move to ease rules controlling the use of pesticides and herbicides, which help fight pests and weeds.

Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.

Industry observers note that the European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default. Safety reviews would only be done in exceptional cases, and regulatory authorities, not the industry, would bear responsibility.

Sources indicate that the commission has said its goal is to cut costs, simplify work for authorities and help farmers stay competitive. Scientists and doctors, however, warn that concerns over human health and environmental impact from these toxic substances are being brushed aside.

The European Commission has noted it's responding to complaints from farmers and the agriculture industry to clarify EU rules that govern pesticide use.

A joint statement released in May by 19 food associations, including CropLife Europe, which promotes pesticides, stated complicated administrative procedures and a lengthy approvals process meant farmers were "left without any effective solutions to protect their crops against insects, weeds and diseases," putting food security and livelihoods at risk.

"The existing system of periodic renewal assessment of every active substance has become unsustainable," the commission's press service told DW, citing "chronic delays" and "bottlenecks" in the approval of upcoming, more sustainable products.

In recent negotiations, EU member states said open-ended authorizations should be restricted to "low-risk active substances.".

But their stance is still wanting to extend initial approval periods for other substances to up to 15 years, and a maximum of 25 years for renewals.

It has been revealed that herbert Dorfmann, a center-right Italian member of the European Parliament, mentioned there is right now a yearslong delay in approving upcoming pesticides, including more eco-friendly options, meaning farmers are forced to rely on older substances. Or, if these are banned, go without altogether.

The commission wants to "make the system more efficient and responsive," while guaranteeing that "the protection of human and animal health and the environment remain the highest priorities.".

Dorfmann, who as co-rapporteur is responsible for interinstitutional negotiations on the issue, backs the commission's stance, saying the EU needs "to open up the system for innovation.".

He aims to bring the parliament's proposal on the new pesticide rules to a vote among EU lawmakers before the end of the year.

Ecologists and medical experts, however, have spoken out forcefully against the proposed changes, saying the potential implications for human health and the environment are being downplayed.

In September, more than 500 experts from across the EU signed an open letter calling on the European Parliament to suspend its consideration of the new regulations and conduct an independent investigation into health and environmental impacts.

On October 7, UN rights experts also backed the call for a full review into whether the proposed changes violated the EU's obligations under international human rights law, especially with regard to agricultural workers and children.

According to recent reports, pesticides can persist in the environment, contaminating water and degrading soils. They can also drive biodiversity loss and poison other animals higher up the food chain.

When it comes to humans, the European Environment Agency has said it was "not yet possible to estimate the burden of disease linked to current levels of exposure to all pesticides.".

However, exposure to chemical pesticides, including banned substances that still persist in the environment, has been linked to various cancers, chronic respiratory disease, neurological disorders and developmental delays, as well as problems with fertility and behavior.

And exposure is widespread: A survey conducted between 2014 and 2021 found that 84% of urine samples from both children and adults in five European countries contained residue from two or more pesticides.

Martina Vijver, scientific director and ecotoxicology expert at Leiden University in the Netherlands, said experts were "deeply concerned" that the EU's current strategy "will weaken rather than strengthen the level of protection for pesticide regulation.".

Speaking at the European Parliament in September, she noted regular reassessments were key to evaluating the safety of pesticides with newly introduced findings, pointing out that the perception of risk changes over time.

"The regulatory system must remain capable of correcting yesterday's decisions with tomorrow's knowledge," she remarked.

Salome Roynel, a policy officer at the Pesticide Action Network Europe, an NGO based in Brussels, said the harmful effects of pesticides aren't often fully understood until years later, when the product is up for reconsideration.

"New science emerges all the time," she told DW, highlighting how 56 active substances have been banned in the EU since 2011 as a result of periodic reviews.

That includes the insecticide chlorpyrifos, previously used in orchards and on vegetable and cereal crops, which has been tied to harmful effects on children's brain development.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel stated it was "obvious that there was some kind of alignment" between the changes proposed by the EU institutions and the demands of the pesticide lobby.

This echoes a new report by nonprofit research and campaign group Corporate Europe Observatory, which remarked Dorfmann and other lawmakers had "copy-pasted […] industry demands" into their regulatory proposals.

Dorfmann denied the lobby influence, telling DW he had met with "both sides, industry and environmental associations," in public debates on the concern.

"The main objective is not to keep old products in the market. The main objective is to bring new ones to the market," Dorfmann noted.

Part of that plan, he added, would be to help more environmentally friendly "biocontrol" products and low-risk substances to bypass current administrative hurdles and get on the market faster.

It's an idea previously championed by Vijver, who agrees that the current system means more environmentally friendly pesticides are stuck in an administrative "traffic jam." She told DW that biocontrol products could go in a green "bus lane" to ease the way to approval at the European Food Safety Authority, while maintaining crucial safety reviews to filter out the more dangerous products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel also supports the plan to speed up approval for biocontrol substances, but said it needs to be part of a wider system change that includes financial support, monitoring and training to use these upcoming products, as well as maintaining the restrictions on more harmful chemical pesticides ― not further deregulation.

"If farmers get easier access to synthetic pesticides tomorrow, they would have no incentive to switch to biocontrol," she said. "It's notable to put [biocontrol pesticides] on the market and we fully support that, but… it will not be the silver bullet.".

Donyell Malen bagged four goals to give Roma their 5-1 victory away to Parma, with Rodrigo Mora also on target, but Wesley was decisive too with a hand in four goals.

The Giallorossi received a massive boost with the return of Paulo Dybala and Mile Svilar, the goalkeeper after nearly two months out, with Manu Koné and Gianluca Mancini also recovered after missing international duty, leaving only Devyne Rensch and Lorenzo Pellegrini on the treatment table.

According to recent reports, the Ducali had shown improvement under coach Alberto Gilardino, but the early Abdoulaye Ndiaye red card saw them lose to Bologna. He was therefore suspended, with David Romero and Dominik Drobnic out, plus Diego Carlos and Adrian Bernabé not at 100 per cent.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Mariano Troilo stung Svilar’s gloves at the near post in the opening 60 seconds, but a few minutes later the goalkeeper rushed out to gather a loose ball and was visibly struggling with a muscular twinge, although he insisted on staying on the field.

Koné went down far too easily when feeling Troilo’s hand on his shoulder, while Leonardo Balerdi threw himself in the path of an El Bilal Touré finish from 12 yards.

Defensive bodies were also vital to stop Enrico Delprato turning in from six yards on an Emanuele Valeri cross, but on the resulting corner, Svilar made a sensational reaction save on the Giovanni Fabbian header from point-blank range.

Mario Hermoso blasted just over from the edge of the box, and Giovanni Daffara was brave off his line to smother a Dybala pass at the feet of Donyell Malen, getting a shinpad in the head for his trouble.

Recent findings suggest that roma did break the deadlock with a moment of pure class from Malen. He hooked the Emanuele Lulli cross out of the air with his back to goal, knocking it down so it was in the right place as he turned to sweep in from 10 yards.

Mancini and Touré got into an argument with some possible hair-pulling and arm-flailing, but on the stroke of half-time a desperate clearance prevented Malen meeting the Rodrigo Mora low cross from six yards.

Daffara flew to parry the Dybala effort after a Malrn back-heel flick, but just as Roma were pouring forward, they were beaten on the counter-attack.

Leonardo Balerdi felt that he had the loose ball under control, but Elphege flicked it away to sprint from the centre-circle and beat the on-rushing Svilar.

Daffara made a magnificent reaction save to push the Mancini header out from under the bar on a Roma corner, but Malen could not turn down the gift from Troilo.

The defender made a complete mess of trying to clear the Wesley cross from the right, so it bobbled into the path of the Dutchman to fire in from six yards.

Moments later, there was a very similar goal again prompted by substitute Wesley’s pull-back from the right, it took a deflection and Rodrigo Mora pounced to tap in from close range.

The introduction of Brazil international Wesley really was transformative, as he provided another assist, rolling across from the right for Malen to complete his hat-trick.

Matias Soulé tested Daffara from distance, as did Hans Nicolussi Caviglia at the other end with Svilar.

It wasn’t over, as Malen scored his fourth of the game when Wesley won it back in midfield and placed a perfectly-weighted pass to send him sprinting, took a touch to get around Daffara, and placed the finish into the tiny sliver of goal remaining as defenders scrambled back to cover.

Malen 39, 68, 77, 90 (R), Elphege 54 (P), Mora 71 (R).

It has been revealed that first launched in 1995, Mitreâs Ultimax ball promptly became a defining symbol in English football. A fixture on Premier League pitches throughout the 1990s, it made history as the first football to break the 100mph speed barrier.

Now, 30 years later, Mitre has reimagined the legendary ball, bringing it back with a modern twist.

The latest Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

Industry observers note that while the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. Hyperflow grooves reduce drag and a sleek pearl finish offers a nod to traditional 30th-anniversary gifts. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has launched the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the latest wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.

The trio, each in vintage 95/96 kits, embody the connection between the past and the future â just as the new Ultimax Pro does itself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:39 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:02 EST, 21 November 2026.

Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks revealed how his picks changed.

It has been revealed that on Friday, speaking about this concern, Arteta stated: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game.

Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal.

According to recent reports, 'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something newly introduced.

In a recent development, 'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put latest things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'.

Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

Chelsea had a similar issue this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

Tech Report: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • It has been revealed that the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

It has been revealed that the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, states she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

"That's the bad news," said marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

Underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

Recent findings suggest that around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," stated Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

Sources indicate that but the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

In a recent development, through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

In a recent development, "Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he remarked.

The collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

In a recent development, "We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig mentioned.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing new ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

Industry observers note that "Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she mentioned.

According to recent reports, "The big advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar said they right now "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

Thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

Recent findings suggest that they then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the new crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

"We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen said. "It's looking really good.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gian Piero Gasperini sees Roma ‘confidence’ growing after their 5-1 victory in Parma, and explains why four-goal hero Donyell Malen has been so unstoppable in Serie A. ‘He fits with our style of football.’.

The Giallorossi maintained their two-point gap from Serie A leaders Lazio thanks to what ultimately turned into a comfortable jaunt at the Stadio Tardini this evening, with Malen scoring four goals around the Rodrigo Mora effort.

Nesta Elphege had temporarily managed to draw Parma level on the counter-attack, but it spurred Roma into a strong response.

“I am very happy, because there is always some uncertainty when players go off and return at the last minute,” Gasperini told DAZN Italia.

“We wanted to see if we could pick up where we left off, and the result doesn’t reflect how difficult today’s match was. Parma were very determined, started strong, but over the course of the 90 minutes we took more control, albeit not as much as the result would suggest.”.

The Giallorossi have 36 goals in the opening 12 Serie A rounds, more than any other team in the last 76 years, since Inter and Milan got 38 and Juventus 37, all in 1950/51.

Malen alone is responsible for 12 of those goals, but if we look at the calendar year since his arrival from Aston Villa in January, the Dutchman has 26 Serie A goals in 2026.

That is an all-time club record, jointly with Pedro Manfredini in 1960, but it is still only November 21 and there are a lot more games to be played.

“We can always improve, both individually and as a team, but undoubtedly this side is growing. We conceded a bad goal at a tough moment of the match, but I saw a strong reaction from the team, and that shows the confidence is there.

“When we are faced with a negative or unlucky moment, we have the confidence to keep playing and get over it.”.

Malen has scored three hat-tricks in 2026 for Roma, and curiously the last player to achieve this in Serie A was also under Gasperini, namely Josip Ilicic for Atalanta.

“Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, you don’t play at that level without quality. Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way.

Recent findings suggest that “There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents, and of course Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary. He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn’t fit as well with our style of football,” concluded Gasperini.

Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S.
  • Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives.
  • Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The big-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Recent findings suggest that researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, states Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

“Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really significant deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

The earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

While looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

According to recent reports, eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, states co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

Recent findings suggest that the ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, notes Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

Sources indicate that the multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

  • Suarez received an eight-match ban and a £40,000 fine for his actions which tarnished his legacy in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been several racist incidents that have marred matches between Liverpool and Manchester United which is usually one of the most must-watch fixtures in club football.

According to recent reports, none more so than back in 2011 when Luis Suarez racially abused Patrice Evra during a 1-1 draw at Anfield. While tempers often flare between both sets of players, resorting to racism is cowardly and an glitch that football still needs to prevent from surfacing on the pitch.

Suarez received an eight-match ban and a £40,000 fine for his actions which tarnished his legacy in the Premier League. Whenever he played a game at Old Trafford thereafter, he was heavily booed by home fans for the incident.

If you asked most if not all, United fans, they wouldn't even sign Suarez in his prime for the current team that sits in the relegation zone in November 2026. But there have been several players who have played for both clubs during their careers and one landed himself in as much trouble as the Uruguayan striker.

The name Peter Beardsley is well known to English football fans because of his legendary playing career both at Newcastle United and Liverpool. He cemented himself as a hero at St James' Park and also earned fan favourite status during his four years at Anfield.

Some fans might be unaware that Beardsley actually played for Manchester United before joining the Magpies and the Reds. That's because he only made one competitive first-team appearance, coming on as a substitute in a League Cup match against Bournemouth in October 1982.

Recent findings suggest that beardsley struggled to break into the senior team and then-manager Ron Atkinson decided against making a conditional transfer permanent. A six-month spell with the Red Devils was spent mostly in the reserves before he became a household name in English football.

In a recent development, after becoming an England international, winning two First Division league titles and the FA Cup with Liverpool, he called time on his playing career in 1999 at the age of 38. Sir Alex Ferguson once admitted he considered trying to bring him back to Old Trafford in September 1992 while he struggled at Everton but a return didn't come to fruition.

Sources indicate that beardsley didn't bid farewell to football after retiring and instead continued in the sport as an assistant coach to the late Kevin Keegan. He eventually took on the same role at Newcastle before coaching the youth teams at St James' Park.

That was until March 2019 when he left his role as coach of the U23 team to supposedly 'seek a new challenge'. This came amid allegations of bullying and an investigation into his conduct, which he denied.

Sources indicate that in September 2019, the FA banned Beardsley from football for 32 weeks after finding him guilty of three charges of racially abusing black players. An independent panel found that he had called a player of black African origin a monkey during a game of head tennis.

It has been revealed that beardsley was also stated to have told black players 'you should be used to that' when they took part in a team-building trip to outdoor adventure park Go Ape. His comments were deemed 'obviously racist and wholly unnaceptable.".

Recent findings suggest that the panel weren't of the belief that Beardsley was a racist, saying in a statement: "We are satisfied that Mr Beardsley is not a racist in the sense of being ill-disposed to persons on grounds of their race or ethnicity. It is also relevant that he has not had the benefit of training and education about offensive racist remarks and the importance of not making them.".

Beardsley noted in a statement provided by his solicitors that he had been “very surprised and disappointed by the decision." They alleged that it was "almost impossible" for him to clear his name because of the "serious flaws and contamination of evidence" during the disciplinary process.

Keegan, John Barnes, Les Ferdinand and Andrew Cole were among the names whom his legal team cited as fellow professionals who offered him their support. Despite the panel determining that he wasn't a racist, the findings have resulted in him not returning to coaching and instead making rare appearances at events.

  • The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

Sources indicate that the company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

Sources indicate that "The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act swiftly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz remarked in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

Here are some of the key Q3 figures:.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing looks to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

CEO Oliver Blume aims to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the proposal, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz said the figures revealed the urgency underlying these looks, saying the company needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz remarked the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he stated.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 10:47 EST, 21 November 2026.

Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne - with the striker revealing he will only return for 'the business end of the season'.

Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.

The defender had won the ball but caught Kane with his follow through on his ankle.

Kane had initially tried to play on after treatment, before eventually needing to be replaced.

The Ballon d'Or winner was upbeat on Saturday morning however, sharing a message with his fans that stressed his readiness to come back better than ever.

Sources indicate that 'The highs and lows of life!' Kane captioned a picture of himself wearing a protective boot. 'Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going in 2027.

Harry Kane was forced off during Bayern Munich's draw against Cologne on Friday night.

Bayern confirmed the England captain is set to be out for months following the injury.

But despite his injury, Kane was upbeat as he spoke to fans for the first time on Saturday (Source: Harry Kane/X).

'I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

'"Tough times don't last, tough people do" - my guy (Julian Edelman) told me this one!' Kane added, quoting the NFL icon.

'Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut (red heart emoji, strong arm emoji).'.

Speaking post-match, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl revealed that Kane has suffered ligament damage.

A Bayern club statement confirmed the blow, reading: 'Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

'This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department.

Industry observers note that 'The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months. Get well soon Harry.'.

Kane's absence will be a major blow for Bayern, with the Ballon d'Or winner having scored ten goals in 16 matches so far this season.

Bayern, who are already without Luis Diaz, Saibari and Serge Gnabry, also saw Michael Olise come off at half-time.

The German giants later confirmed Olise had suffered a 'contusion of the forefoot', with the Frenchman set to undergo treatment in the coming days.

It remains to be seen whether Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week when making his 126th appearance in the 2-1 win over Croatia - is at risk of missing the Nations League quarter-final against Norway in March.

Vincent Kompany, who was back in the dugout for the first time since his collapse last month, admitted other players will have to step up for Bayern in the absence of star names such as Kane.

'These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now,' Kompany said, as per Bild.

'We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern.

Bayern were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Vincent Kompany's return to the touchline.

Industry observers note that 'We will all try together to make this situation a positive one for ourselves. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too.'.

Bayern were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne, with Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore giving the visitors a shock first half lead at the Allianz Arena.

Nathaniel Brown drew Bayern level before half-time, but the hosts were unable to find a winner on Kompany's return.

The draw gives Borussia Dortmund the chance to move to the top of the Bundesliga table on Saturday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rio Ferdinand has weighed in on the controversy surrounding Bayern Munich's handling of Jamal Musiala after FIFPRO raised concerns over comments made by the club's hierarchy.

In a recent development, musiala's long-term health has become an issue for Bayern, who have publicly and internally debated whether the German can return to his best. The young attacker collapsed during pre-season friendlies in the summer and has since confirmed he is managing a neurological dysfunction with medication.

Industry observers note that the 23-year-old's health issues have prevented him from playing regularly so far this season, limiting him to five appearances. He returned from a torn muscle fiber that had sidelined him for around two months when he came off the bench in Friday's 1-1 draw against FC Koln.

Sources indicate that musiala's long-term future in football became the subject of intense speculation, with rumours circulating online about a potential imminent retirement. Those claims were proven untrue, but Bayern's higher-ups have still voiced concerns over whether he can recapture the form he showed prior to his illness.

Supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge received huge criticism for his comments on the situation. He suggested that the club would be within their rights to question his contract if they felt 'what he’s capable of now isn’t what’s stipulated in the contract.'.

Those comments came after honorary president Uli Hoeneß described Musiala's illness as "not easily curable" and a dilemma for the Bundesliga outfit. At the club's Annual General Meeting on Saturday, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and club president Herbert Hainer confirmed Bayern were unaware of Musiala's condition when signing him to an extension until 2030.

According to recent reports, dreesen and Hainer both denied feeling misled by the player's camp over the newly introduced deal, which runs until 2030. FIFPRO have now condemned those remarks in a statement criticizing the club's treatment of the player.

In noted statement, FIFPRO stated that they are "deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from Bayern Munich's leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury.".

According to recent reports, they added: "Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.".

It has been revealed that "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.".

FIFPRO pointed out that a player's form or an injury does not give a club ground to reopen terms it agreed to: "Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.".

Former Manchester United defender Ferdinand agreed with FIFPRO's stance, in which the players' union also spoke of standing with Musiala and all players who "honour their commitments." He shared his thoughts on Bayern's handling of the Germany international's condition and contract by highlighting player welfare:.

According to recent reports, "Bayern Munich are better than this.... if they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health issues Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media.

He added: "This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly. Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.".

Musiala has been at Bayern since 2019 when he joined the club's youth academy from Chelsea. He became the youngest goalscorer in their history at the age of 17 and 205 days before helping the Bavarians win six Bundesliga titles, the Champions League and the DFB-Pokal.

Max Allegri explained his Napoli transformation ahead of tonight’s meeting with Torino, including the fact Kevin De Bruyne is on the bench. ‘We always look vulnerable.’.

It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT].

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s four Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The Partenopei went into the break for international duty coming off heavy defeats to Juventus and FC Porto, then holding Serie A leaders Lazio to a 1-1 draw.

The injury crisis managed to get even worse, as Alex Meret is out for a couple of months after a fracture in his back, joining Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Alessandro Buongiorno on the treatment table.

“It’s important because we are trailing in the table, we drew the last two home games with Roma and Lazio, so we must try to get back to winning ways,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

“Torino are doing very well, Ignazio Abate is in his first Serie A season as a coach, he has learned a lot already and I am happy for him. We need a lot of precision and technical quality. We’ve got Spinazzola and Favasuli back in the squad, one starts, the other is on the bench.”.

Napoli change system for this game to a 3-5-2, giving Rasmus Hojlund no rest despite featuring on international duty and with the Champions League trip to Manchester City coming up on Tuesday.

It is a further sign of how little trust the club has in Lorenzo Lucca and Noa Lang, who are expected to move on in the January transfer window, as Antonio Vergara is in a new support role.

According to recent reports, “Antonio is a very good player, he can find spaces between the lines, can run into the box. The problem is that we concede too many goals, we don’t give a sense of security when the opponents have the ball, we always look too vulnerable.”.

Kevin De Bruyne is rested initially, as the veteran was also given a couple of extra days off following his two Belgium starts in the Nations League against Turkiye and Italy.

According to recent reports, “He played a lot of games, started both for international duty, tonight the substitutions will be more important than ever. De Bruyne has great technical quality, his fitness has improved a lot, but don’t forget he was out for a very long time.

“We want to see the right approach, and above all to be more practical when we don’t have the ball.”.

India increases growth forecast for fiscal year

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it stated in its October economic review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it stated in its October economic review.

The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.

India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

The report contrasted these figures with global growth predictions of nearer 3%, saying "India's growth momentum, by comparison, has held firm.".

The ministry remarked growth in various key indicators like energy consumption, port traffic, goods and services tax (GST) collections, and car sales had accelerated in the previous quarter.

However, the ministry also warned of continued inflationary pressure and pressure on the rupee currency, as well as downside risks from the El Nino weather phonemenon that could threaten soil moisture ahead of the winter sowing season.

It said that external factors like oil prices and "global uncertainties" — seemingly a reference at least in part to the instablity in the Middle East — continued to pressure the rupee's value and pose inflationary risks.

Consumer price inflation (CPI), the wholesale price index (WPI), food cost prices and fuel and power prices were all rising month for month, albeit at very different rates.

Recent findings suggest that the CPI was up 5.54% year-on-year in September, but the WPI had risen more sharply at 11.39%. Food index inflation was up by 8% in rural areas, and a slightly more modest 7.18% in urban centers.

But, as in many other countries, fuel and power costs increases were in an entirely different league, at 25.85% inflation in September 2026 comapred to the same month a year earlier, prior to the outbreak of fighting in the Middle East.

Although it has been a comparatively slow decline, the rupee has been consistently losing value against the US dollar over the past five years, threatening the country's relative purchasing power internationally. This slide has picked up pace in the last 15 months or so.

But the ministry pointed to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion and mentioned that India was "well-positioned" to weather such risks and sustain its expansionary trajectory..

For a number of years, Wayne Rooney was among the very best players in the Premier League. He won the competition five times at Manchester United and lifted many more major honours under Sir Alex Ferguson.

He also established himself as one of the greatest English footballers of all time, scoring a then-record 53 international goals with the Three Lions. But it all started for the footballer at Everton.

It has been revealed that still just 16 years old, Rooney declared himself to the world with a stunning strike against Arsenal, which instantly went down in Premier League folklore. He played a total of 117 times for the Toffees, across two spells, starring alongside club icons such as Duncan Ferguson, Leighton Baines, and Kevin Campbell.

One of his former teammates, however, retired in 2011 and is now in jail.

Recent findings suggest that li Tie was a defensive midfielder who started out in China at Liaoning FC before being picked up by Everton in 2002. After an initial loan, he signed permanently and went on to play 40 times for the Toffees, with 30 appearances coming alongside Rooney.

Former teammate David Unsworth once noted:.

“He was tidy on the ball, skilful, he fitted right in. He didn’t try and segregate himself as a foreign player, he enjoyed the banter and had a laugh. He was an absolute diamond of a bloke.”.

Li left Goodison Park in 2006, but stayed in England for two more seasons, playing just once for Sheffield United due to an injury. He then returned to China, playing for Chengdu Blades and Liaoning Whowin before retiring in 2011. Sadly, injury challenges were to blame again.

It has been revealed that despite his fitness struggles across his career, he still played 92 times for his country, making him China's 11th-most-capped men's player in history. After hanging up his boots, he later got into coaching, but this is where his troubles started.

After spells in charge of Hebei China Fortune and Wuhan Zall, Li served asinterim manager from 2019, taking over from Marcello Lippi, before being appointed permanently in 2020 and leaving the post in 2021.

A year after he left his post, China’s public prosecutor put out a bombshell statement which accused Li of ‘accepting and offering bribes’ to an array of individuals, including non-state employees:.

"Li Tie, the former head coach of the Chinese national men’s football team, was suspected of accepting bribes, offering bribes, offering bribes at the unit, accepting bribes of non-state employees, and offering bribes to non-state employees.”.

It has been revealed that in 2024, he made a televised confession, admitting to the match-fixing despite knwiing that people found guilty and convicted of corruption in his country have been given long prison sentences. His statement read:.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm very sorry. I should have kept my head to the ground and followed the right path. There were certain things that at the time were common practices in football. By gaining 'success' through such improper means, it actually made me more and more impatient and eager for quick results.".

Industry observers note that he added: "In order to achieve good performance, I resorted to influencing referees, bribing opposing players and coaches, sometimes through clubs dealing with other clubs. This behaviour becomes a habit, and eventually, there is even a slight dependence on these practices.".

The former Everton player admittedhe paid £330,000 (3 million yuan) in bribes to become manager of the Chinese national team, and added that match-fixing was rife throughout his two promotions with Hebei China Fortune and Wuhan Zall.

A court in Hubei province alleged that from 2015, when he was an assistant coach at the Hebei China Fortune club, until 2021, when he quit as China coach, Li gave and received bribes totalling 120 million yuan ($16.5 million). In exchange for bribes, the court remarked, Li would select certain individuals for the national team as well as help clubs win competitions and sign players.

His punishment was severe, as he was sentenced to 20 years in prison for giving and receiving bribes. Not only that, but in 2026, while still locked away, he was also given a lifetime ban by the Chinese Football Association for match-fixing.
